subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should scoped ACP permission defaults be exposed as a generic `permissionProfile` contract on `bindings[].acp` and `agents.list[].runtime.acp`, or as ACPX-specific `permissionMode` and `nonInteractivePermissions` keys?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable public config shape controls security boundaries and could either align with current generic runtime options or duplicate ACPX-specific plugin config.

options.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
options.body: Add scoped `permissionProfile` defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option alias layer, keeping ACPX-specific names at the plugin-global layer.

options.title: Add ACPX-specific scoped keys
options.body: Implement the requested `permissionMode` and optional `nonInteractivePermissions` precedence directly for ACPX sessions, accepting a backend-specific config surface.

options.title: Keep global config only
options.body: Document `/acp permissions` and global ACPX config as the supported paths and leave static scoped permission defaults out for now.

recommendation.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
recommendation.body: Add scoped `permissionProfile` defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option alias layer, keeping ACPX-specific names at the plugin-global layer.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns both the ACP runtime option shape and the ACPX integration path most likely to define the durable contract.
